transcript.answer: Lore's agent pods run in Kubernetes clusters, as Agent CRs with agent and station pods that a controller manages. In the minikube dev setup that controller lives in the separate ai-agent-subsystem. The Lore Floor does not hold a Kubernetes client to start them. ADR-044 extracted a per-cluster `cluster-agent` app (`apps/cluster-agent`) as the only process holding a Kubernetes client. The Floor and other callers go through it over bearer-authed HTTP domain operations under `/api/cluster`. The cluster-agent reports terminal Agent CR phases back through the event-router's `POST /api/events`. This is what allows more than one execution cluster. Older code did use `@kubernetes/client-node` directly in the Floor, as issue 891 describes. The later ADR-024 amendment and PR 2484 moved cluster authority to the cluster-agent. I did not verify the exact current state of every call site.

judgements.reason: The answer says Lore's own `apps/cluster-agent` holds a Kubernetes client and runs the pods; the gold says the pods run in the external re-cinq/floor, reached only via @re-cinq/floor-client, and Lore holds no Kubernetes client.
